founderLine: Adds ready-made examples for connecting your agents to Sentry for errors, and to SigNoz or Dynatrace for logs and metrics, while they work an incident.
whyItFits: AURA's agents reach production tools through MCP, and the README's integrations table has no Sentry, SigNoz or Dynatrace. incident-response-datadog.toml already shows the pattern to copy, and SigNoz and Dynatrace Managed fit your self-hosted users.
risks: None to existing configs: these are new examples, and the README only gains rows. Sentry's and SigNoz's servers also have write tools, so the Sentry example leaves out the skill that updates issues and the SigNoz example filters to read tools; PagerDuty stays unfiltered, as in the sibling examples. A server that can't start within AURA's connect timeout shows as failed and the agent carries on without it, so the examples say what to pull or install ahead of time. Dynatrace Managed needs Node.js 26 (26.12.1 or later), as its package requires, and its tools answer without an error when they can't reach the cluster, so an agent with bad settings can read that as nothing being wrong.
rollback: Delete the new examples and their README rows.

vendor.claim: Sentry's and SigNoz's official servers and Dynatrace's own, community-supported server, all listed in the MCP Registry
